title: personal-okr-weekly-checkin-amelia-ross-2026-03-25
content:
Week: 2026-03-24 -> 2026-03-25
Owner: Amelia Ross (eng-serving-runtime)
Purpose: weekly personal OKR check-in + quick retro / action items  - lightweight scratchpad.

Summary / headline
- Progress: Canary rollout of batching-scheduler v2 is on track (canary pool at 10%); initial telemetry looks good.
- Risk: p95 tail still spiking on multi-tenant bursts; need one more iteration on priority preemption to hit KR2.
- Blockers: infra quota for additional dedicated pool (billing/infra approval pending).

OKRs (current quarter)
- O1: Reduce production p95 inference latency for hosted-api p50->p95 gap by 35%
  - KR1: Deploy batching-scheduler v2 to canary and validate with synthetic traffic (target: 20% latency reduction at 95th)
  - KR2: Implement priority preemption to bound tail-latency (target: p95 < 120ms for baseline loads)
  - KR3: Add cold-start cache priming for new model instances (target: reduce cold-start p99 by 60%)

Progress notes against KRs
- KR1 (batching-scheduler v2): Canary at 10% traffic since Fri 2026-03-20. Observed 18% improvement median, ~15-22% improvement at p95 across models tested.
  - Next: expand canary to 30% after extra validation run on Tues 3/26.
  - Tests run: qps sweep + variable sequence lengths (confluence: kv-cache-rollout notes).
- KR2 (priority preemption): Initial design review done with SRE (Jordan). Prototype in PR #701.
  - Current: Preemption reduces queue buildup but in some burst shapes we still see p95 spikes ~140-160ms.
  - Hypothesis: preemption logic currently uses simple token-window; need to incorporate model-weighted slots / per-customer budgeting.
  - Action: Spike implementation for model-weighted slots (ETA 1 week).
- KR3 (cold-start): Cache priming experiment launched for small model family; results promising (cold-start p99 down ~50%) but needs integration tests for memory safety.

Quantitative metrics (latest telemetry)
- Hosted API aggregate (last 7d):
  - tokens served: "~1.1B"
  - avg cost per 1M tokens (approx): "$5.60"
  - p50 latency: 40ms, p95 latency: 132ms, p99 latency: 480ms
  - error rate (4xx/5xx): 0.23% (up from 0.18% last week; investigating client-side retries)
- Canary (batching-scheduler v2):
  - p95: 105-115ms vs baseline 130-140ms (model dependent)
  - throughput: +12% effective tokens/sec in steady state

Recent activities this week
- Mon: design review with SRE (Jordan) on preemption; split tasks and set milestones for PR #701.
- Tue: ran synthetic ramp tests for canary; verified throughput improvements; documented test harness (linked PR).
- Wed: paired with Samira on telemetry dashboards; added per-route waterfall and token-cost breakdown.
- Thu: meeting with infra/billing to request extra quota for dedicated canary pool; waiting on approval.
- Fri: retro + notes to self -> iterate on preemption algorithm.

Blockers / Risks
- Infra quota limit blocking expansion of canary to 30% (impact: slower validation, delayed rollout). Owner: Amelia -> escalate to infra ops and finance.
- Tail latency variance on mixed workloads (edge case with long-generation tokens). Owner: Jordan -> propose model-weighted slots.
- Manual rollout steps still touch sensitive config; need a small automation script to reduce human error. Owner: Amelia -> backlog.

Action items (this week / next)
- [ ] Expand canary to 30% after synthetic validation (ETA 2026-03-26)  - assignee: Amelia
- [ ] Implement model-weighted slots prototype and measure tail-latency impact (ETA 1 week)  - assignee: Jordan + Amelia
- [ ] Follow up with infra/billing on quota approval (due 2026-03-26)  - assignee: Amelia (escalate to finance if no response)
- [ ] Add test for cold-start memory safety and run integration test (ETA 2026-03-28)  - assignee: Samira
- [ ] Add small automation to rollouts to reduce manual steps (low effort)  - assignee: Amelia

Notes to self / scratchpad
- Check GH PR comments on #701 by EOD Mon; merge gating depends on one more benchmark (p95 tail under mixed model load).
- Consider flagging short sequences differently in scheduler to avoid wasting large batch slots.
- Revisit cost impact: if throughput gains hold, projected monthly savings ~6-8% for hosted API token cost for the impacted models.

Loose thoughts / brainstorms (non-actionable)
- Could we integrate a small RL-based admission controller that learns to balance latency vs throughput by route? Maybe too heavy for this quarter but interesting for Optimize roadmap.
- Expose a per-customer soft-priority credit so customers can buy lower tail-latency (revenue + predictability).

References / links
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/kv-cache-rollout
- Jira: ENG-4823 (batching-scheduler v2), ENG-4899 (priority-preemption)
- GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/701

Quick retro (what went well / what to improve)
- Went well: cross-team pairing (SRE + telemetry) moved a lot of signal quickly. Canary telemetry gave early confidence.
- Improve: need faster infra approvals and a small checklist to automate canary expansion without manual ops steps.

End of check-in.

---
Notes: keep this as a living doc; update after Friday retro / Monday follow-ups.
short_summary: Canary rollout of batching-scheduler v2 shows 15-20% p95 improvements; tail-latency still needs work via priority preemption and model-weighted slots. Infra quota is a blocker for expanding canary to 30%.
